Subject: Prostate MRI | Spaarne Gasthuis, Haarlem | 20 January 2025
Clinical Query: Persistent PSA elevation (9.9 ng/mL) and prior scoring.
FINDINGS:
Volumetric assessment yields a gland size of 50.0 mL. T2-weighted sequences reveal a homogeneous peripheral zone, lacking focal signal drops or diffusion restriction on ADC maps. Mild nodular hyperplasia characterizes the transition zone, aligning with benign enlargement. Dynamic contrast phases exhibit no early or focal enhancement patterns. Seminal vesicles maintain normal caliber and signal intensity. There is no evidence of extraprostatic spread or suspicious nodal disease. The bladder wall presents smoothly, free of diverticula.
IMPRESSION:
Benign prostatic enlargement measuring 50.0 mL. No PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion identified. PI-RADS 2.
PSA density: 0.19 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.6607788.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial laboratory screening in February 2024 flagged a PSA reading of 9.3 ng/mL, which triggered a repeat draw and urology referral. Follow-up values temporarily decreased to 6.7 ng/mL during August, before climbing back to 9.9 ng/mL. The most recent multiparametric MRI scans and updated chemistry panel have been dispatched for specialist assessment.
